one_liner: Lock-free recoverable persistent-memory malloc (LRMalloc-based); about 10x faster than PMDK libpmemobj and Makalu on allocator microbenchmarks.
what_it_does: A malloc/free-style allocator for byte-addressable nonvolatile memory (Intel Optane-class DAX files under /mnt/pmem, or /dev/shm when built with SHM_SIMULATING). The C API is RP_init(id, size), RP_malloc, RP_free, RP_calloc, RP_realloc, RP_set_root/RP_get_root (up to 1024 persistent roots), RP_recover and RP_close; after a crash, RP_init reports a restart and RP_recover rebuilds allocator state. It is not a drop-in for PMDK's transactional object API: it gives crash-consistent allocation metadata, not failure-atomic updates of your data.
how_it_is_fast: It reuses LRMalloc's lock-free design (thread-local caches of size-class blocks, 64 KiB superblocks with CAS-updated anchors) and persists only what cannot be rebuilt (superblock descriptors and roots) with clwb/clflush plus fences, keeping free lists and thread caches transient. Instead of logging every allocation like PMDK, recovery after a crash runs a mark-and-sweep garbage collection from the persistent roots, conservative by default or guided by user-supplied filter functions, to reconstruct free lists. Position-independent offset pointers let the heap be remapped at a different address on restart.
when_to_use: Persistent-memory data structures (lock-free queues, maps, trees) that need a non-blocking, crash-recoverable allocator under many threads
Replacing PMDK libpmemobj or Makalu allocation in a research or prototype system where allocation rate is the bottleneck
Small-object workloads: blocks up to about 14 KiB come from size classes (MAX_SZ = 8 KiB + 3 x 2 KiB in pm_config.hpp)
Systems that can tolerate a GC pass at restart in exchange for no per-allocation logging during normal operation
Emulated persistence on DRAM (/dev/shm) for testing persistent algorithms on machines without NVM
when_not_to_use: Ordinary transient heaps: the repo CSVs show it on par with jemalloc at low thread counts and 2-3x slower on Threadtest and Shbench above 48 threads
You need failure-atomic transactions over your own data (PMDK's tx API); Ralloc only keeps allocator metadata consistent
Production use: abandoned since 2020-10-23, open bug #12 on restart with /dev/shm, open issue #15 (only one Ralloc instance per application) and #16 (redundant concurrent heap expansion)
Pure C programs that need precise recovery: the README warns filter functions are not supported in pure C, leaving only conservative GC
Very high thread counts with the bundled LRMalloc build: hazard counter overflow and segfaults reported above about 72 threads (README warning)

integration.dependencies: libjemalloc (necessary per README, used for transient allocations), pthread, libatomic; PMDK and Makalu only to run the comparison benchmarks
integration.platforms: Linux x86-64 (clwb/clflush inline asm, MAP_SYNC DAX mapping at /mnt/pmem or /dev/shm emulation)
integration.thread_safety: Lock-free and thread-safe; threads should be created through RP_pthread_create (pm_thread_create) so thread caches are handled
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial - malloc-like RP_* calls replace pmemobj_alloc/Makalu allocation, but roots, recovery and filter functions differ and PMDK transactions have no equivalent

gotchas: The heap path is compiled in: without SHM_SIMULATING files go to /mnt/pmem/ (edit src/pm_config.hpp for another mount); RP_init defaults to a 5 GiB heap and regions grow in 1 GiB steps
Pointers stored in the persistent heap must be reachable from RP_set_root roots or they are reclaimed by the recovery GC after a crash
Conservative recovery treats any word that looks like a heap pointer as live, so it can leak blocks; precise filter functions are C++ only
The benchmark 'lr' build is Ralloc with -DPWB_IS_NOOP (no flushes or fences), not upstream LRMalloc; read the repo CSV labels with that in mind
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No catalogued sibling targets persistent memory; pick Ralloc only when allocations must survive crashes, and pick mimalloc-class allocators such as those in this category (SpeedMalloc, v8malloc, Mesh) for ordinary transient heaps, where Ralloc trails jemalloc at high thread counts.
verified_claims_summary: The ISMM 2020 paper (seen via search snippet, PDF blocked here) reports about 10x over Makalu and PMDK on Threadtest and Shbench and up to 37x over Makalu on Larson; the repo's own CSVs agree (Threadtest 1 thread 28.7 s vs Makalu 298 s and PMDK 1690 s; Larson 88 threads 4.8e8 ops vs Makalu 1.27e7, derived from page data), built with GCC -O3 per test/Makefile, CPU model not stated in the repo.
status_note: Abandoned research code (last commit 2020-10-23, open restart bug #12) but MIT-licensed and small enough to vendor for persistent-memory prototypes.
